A three-time [[NBA All-Star]] and a two-time member of the [[All-NBA Team]], he was awarded the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] in 2021. In his only season of [[college basketball]] with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], Randle was named a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the first round of the [[2014 NBA draft]] with the seventh overall pick. In his regular season debut, Randle broke his right leg and missed the remainder of his rookie season. After four years with the Lakers, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He has also played for the [[New York Knicks]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG Julius Randle reverse dunk (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Randle performs a reverse [[Slam dunk|dunk]] during the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Randle attended [[Prestonwood Christian Academy]] in [[Plano, Texas]], where he was widely regarded as a top 5 player in the class of 2013 with [[Andrew Wiggins]], [[Jabari Parker]], [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], and [[Aaron Gordon]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2752 |title=Rivals150 for the Class of 2013 |work=Yahoo.com |access-date=January 3, 2013}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/class/2013 |title=2013 ESPN 100 |work=ESPN.com |access-date=January 3, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2013 |title=SCOUT.COM COLLEGE BASKETBALL TEAM RECRUITING PROSPECTS – 2013 |work=Scout.com |access-date=January 3, 2013}} In August 2012, Randle won the Under Armour Elite 24 dunk Contest{{cite web|last=Zagoria |first=Adam |url=http://zagsblog.com/articles/randle-wins-elite-24-dunk-contest-frankamp-takes-3-point-contest/ |title=Randle Wins Elite 24 Dunk Contest; Frankamp Takes 3-Point Contest |work=ZagsBlog.com |date=August 25, 2012 |access-date=January 3, 2013}} and the next day he was named one of the MVPs of the Elite 24 game, where he scored 27 points and led his team to a 164–138 victory.{{cite web|last=Osborne |first=Ben |url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/aaron-gordon-julius-randle-star-in-under-armour-elite-24-game/ |title=Aaron Gordon and Julius Randle Star In Under Armour Elite 24 Game |work=SLAMOnline.com |date=August 26, 2012 |access-date=January 3, 2013}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Randle was listed as the No. 1 power forward and the No. 2 player in the nation in 2013.{{cite web |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/108009 |title=Julius Randle |work=Rivals.com |access-date=February 22, 2016 |archive-date=August 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220822150057/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/108009 |url-status=dead }} The weekend after [[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving]] in his senior season, Randle fractured his foot playing in a tournament and missed three months as a result. In March 2013, Randle returned for the [[Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools|TAPPS]] 5A playoffs and led his team to its third state title in four years.{{cite web|last=Zagoria |first=Adam |url=http://zagsblog.com/articles/julius-randle-out-3-months-with-fractured-foot/ |title=Julius Randle Out 3 Months With Fractured Foot; Parker Visits BYU |work=ZagsBlog.com |date=November 26, 2012 |access-date=January 3, 2013}} As a senior in 2012–13, Randle averaged 32.5 points and 22.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Julius Randle - Men's Basketball |url=https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/julius-randle/748 |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |date=August 10, 2017 |access-date=February 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224210759/https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/julius-randle/748 |archive-date=February 24, 2021}} On March 20, 2013, Randle committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], choosing it over [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. He then joined twin brothers [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew]] and [[Aaron Harrison]], [[James Young (basketball)|James Young]], [[Dakari Johnson]] and [[Marcus Lee]] as the sixth incoming Kentucky player selected to play in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], as well as the [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|2013 Jordan Brand Classic]]. In 2023, PCA would retire his #30, the first number to be retired by the school for any former athlete.{{Cite web |date=2023-08-26 |title=Knicks' Julius Randle Earns 'Great Honor' & Surprise From High School |url=https://www.si.com/nba/knicks/onsi/news/new-york-knicks-julius-randle-high-school-number-retirement |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=New York Knicks On SI |language=en-US}} ==College career== On February 28, 2014, Randle was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx |work=NaismithAwards.com |access-date=February 18, 2014 |date=February 28, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006124015/http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }} He went on to help Kentucky reach the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship game]], which they lost to the University of Connecticut. He ended the [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2013–14]] season with 24 double-doubles, the second most double-doubles by a UK player in school history, behind [[Dan Issel]]'s 25 in 1969–70, and the most double-doubles by a UK freshman (the previous record was shared by [[DeMarcus Cousins]] and [[Anthony Davis]] at 20). In 40 games (all starts), he averaged 15.0 points, 10.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 30.8 minutes per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/julius-randle-1.html |title=Julius Randle Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=January 3, 2014}} On April 22, 2014, Randle declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Tucker | first=Kyle |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/04/22/kentuckys-julius-randle-declares-for-the-nba-draft/8005193/ |title=Kentucky's Julius Randle declares for the NBA draft |work=USAToday.com |date=April 22, 2014 |access-date=April 22, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2014–2018)=== Randle was selected with the seventh overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|last=Trudell|first=Mike|title=The Newest Laker: Julius Randle|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/140626juliusrandle_7th|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=July 19, 2014}} On October 28, 2014, after only 14 minutes of official NBA playing time, Randle broke his right tibia during the [[2014–15 Los Angeles Lakers season|Lakers' 2014–15]] season opener against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite news|last1=Holmes|first1=Baxter|title=Julius Randle likely out for season|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/11783195/julius-randle-los-angeles-lakers-suffers-serious-right-leg-injury-opener|access-date=October 29, 2014|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2014}} He underwent successful surgery the following day to repair the fracture,{{cite news|title=Julius Randle has Successful Surgery|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/141029randle_surgery|access-date=October 29, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2014}} and subsequently missed the rest of the season. On March 9, 2015, he was cleared for full weight-bearing, non-contact basketball activities.{{cite news|last=Ramirez|first=Joey|title=Randle Cleared for Non-Contact Basketball Activities|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/practice/150309_injuryreport|access-date=March 10, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=March 9, 2015}} Randle returned to action in July 2015 with the Lakers' [[2015 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] team.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25245403/summer-league-eye-openers-mudiay-shines-randle-not-so-much|title=Summer League eye-openers: Mudiay shines, Julius Randle not so much|work=CBSSports.com|date=July 21, 2015|access-date=July 21, 2015}} Exactly a year after injuring himself in his NBA debut, Randle had 15 points and 11 rebounds as a starter in a 112–111 season-opening loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Wolves edge Lakers 112-111 in first game since Flip's death|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015}} On December 2, he recorded 15 points and a then-career-high 19 rebounds in a 108–104 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151202/LALWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Bryant scores 31 to lead Lakers past Wizards 108-104|work=NBA.com|date=December 2, 2015|access-date=December 2, 2015}} On January 29, 2016, he scored a career-high 23 points in a loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/160129_clippperswrap|title=Randle Scores Career-High in Loss to Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 31, 2016}} He matched that mark on March 8, recording 23 points and 11 rebounds in a 107–98 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160308/ORLLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Lakers handle Magic 107-98 for rare back-to-back victories|work=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2016|access-date=March 8, 2016}} On March 25, he recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 13 points, 18 rebounds, and a then career-high 10 assists in a 116–105 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. At 21 years old, he became the youngest Lakers player with a triple-double since [[Magic Johnson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160325/DENLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Balanced Nuggets overcome Kobe's 28 to beat Lakers, 116-105|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=March 25, 2016}} Six days later, he hit a game-winning hook shot in the paint with 1.9 seconds left in overtime to lift the Lakers to a 102–100 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160330/MIALAL/gameinfo.html|title=Randle hits big shot in Lakers' 102-100 OT win over Heat|work=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2016|access-date=April 5, 2016}} On April 6, he set a career high with 20 rebounds in a 91–81 loss to the Clippers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160406/LACLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Clippers beat Lakers 91-81 in Kobe's next-to-last home game|work=NBA.com|date=April 6, 2016|access-date=April 7, 2016}} He appeared in all 15 games to begin the 2016–17 season before missing three straight in late November because of a hip injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899713|title=Davis scores 41, Pelicans rout short-handed Lakers 105-88|work=ESPN.com|date=November 29, 2016|access-date=November 30, 2016}} On November 30, 2016, he had 13 points and matched a career high with 20 rebounds in a 96–90 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899719|title=Randle makes late layup to help Lakers edge Bulls 96-90|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=December 1, 2016}} On March 15, 2017, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 139–100 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900405|title=Williams, Harden send Rockets to 139-100 win over Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=March 15, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}} Randle began [[2017–18 Los Angeles Lakers season|2017–18]] as a [[reserve (sport)|reserve]], while [[Larry Nance Jr.]] started at power forward. He excelled as a backup [[center (basketball)|center]] when the team went to a [[small ball (basketball)|small lineup]], and he returned to the starting lineup on December 29, 2017.{{cite news|last=Ganguli|first=Tania|title=Lakers and Spurs re-engage in discussions about Kawhi Leonard, extend qualifying offer to Julius Randle|date=June 27, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-julius-randle-qualifying-20180627-story.html}} On December 31, Randle set season highs with 29 points and 15 rebounds in a 148–142 double overtime loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975286|title=Paul helps Rockets to 148-142 win over Lakers in double OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2017|access-date=December 31, 2017}} On March 11, 2018, he had a career-high 36 points, 14 rebounds, and seven assists in a 127–113 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975746|title=Julius Randle's 36 lead Lakers past LeBron's Cavs, 127-113|work=ESPN.com|date=March 11, 2018|access-date=March 11, 2018}} Randle finished the season as the only Laker to appear in all 82 games. As a starter, he averaged 18.6 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 3.1 assists. He became a [[restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agent]] after the season. ===New Orleans Pelicans (2018–2019)=== On July 2, 2018, the Lakers renounced their rights to Randle, making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23978964/los-angeles-lakers-renounce-julius-randle-agree-terms-rajon-rondo|title=Sources: Lakers renounce Pelicans-bound Julius Randle, agree to deal with Rajon Rondo|work=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018}} On July 9, Randle signed a two-year, $18 million contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-free-agents-elfrid-payton-and-julius-randle|title=Pelicans sign free agents Elfrid Payton and Julius Randle|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}}{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23979595/ex-lakers-center-julius-randle-joining-pelicans-2-year-18m-deal|title=Ex-Lakers center Julius Randle joining Pelicans on 2-year, $18M deal|work=ESPN.com|date=July 3, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}} In his debut for the Pelicans in their season opener on October 17, Randle had 25 points off the bench in a 131–112 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070215|title=Davis, Mirotic lead Pelicans past Rockets 131-112|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}} On November 19, he recorded his sixth career triple-double with 21 points, 14 rebounds and 10 assists in 25 minutes in a 140–126 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070927|title=Davis, Randle lead Pelicans past Spurs, 140-126|work=ESPN.com|date=November 19, 2018|access-date=November 19, 2018}} On December 3, he scored a then career-high 37 points in a 129–126 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071030|title=Harris, Gallinari help Clippers hold off Pelicans 129-126|work=ESPN.com|date=December 3, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}} Two days later, he had 27 points and 18 rebounds in a 132–106 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071044|title=Randle, Davis push Pelicans past Mavericks 132-106|work=ESPN.com|date=December 5, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}} On February 27, 2019, he scored 35 points in a 125–119 loss to the Lakers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071594|title=LeBron's 33 send Lakers past Davis' Pelicans, 125-119|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2019}} On March 15, he scored a career-high 45 points in a 122–110 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071704|title=Lillard leads Blazers past Pelicans 122-110|work=ESPN.com|date=March 15, 2019|access-date=March 16, 2019}} He declined his second-year player option on June 16, 2019, and became a free agent.{{cite web |title=Report: Pelicans' Julius Randle declines player option, enters free agency |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/06/16/report-pelicans-julius-randle-opts-out |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 1, 2020 |date=June 16, 2019}} ===New York Knicks (2019–2024)=== On July 9, 2019, Randle signed a three-year, $63 million contract with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-sign-five-players|title=New York Knicks Sign Five Players|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2019}} On February 16, 2021, Randle scored 44 points and logged a then career-high seven 3-pointers in a 123–112 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |last1=Matange |first1=Yash |title=All-Star Moment of the Night: Julius Randle's season-high 44 points propels Knicks to third straight win |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/all-star-moment-of-the-night-julius-randles-season-high-44-points-propels-knicks-to-third-straight-win/indf8db018nzzna4vuv8q83c |website=NBA.com Canada |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406152449/https://sports.yahoo.com/julius-randle-makes-case-star-063910741.html |url-status=dead }} On February 23, Randle was named as a reserve for the [[2021 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web |title=Harden, Lillard headline 2021 NBA All-Star reserves |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-nba-all-star-reserves-revealed |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 24, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} On April 16, Randle tied his season high 44 points, while also recording 10 rebounds and 7 assists, to lead the Knicks to a 117–109 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |title=Randle scores 44 in hometown, Knicks beat Mavs 117-109 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307650 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 26, 2021 |date=April 16, 2021}} After the end of the regular season, Randle was named the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]], receiving 98 of 100 first place votes.{{cite web |title=Julius Randle named 2020-21 Kia NBA Most Improved Player |url=https://www.nba.com/news/julius-randle-named-2020-21-kia-nba-most-improved-player |website=NBA.com |access-date=May 26, 2021 |date=May 25, 2021}} He was also named to the [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Second Team]] as a forward.{{Cite web |title=Knicks' Julius Randle earns Second Team All-NBA honors |url=https://www.yahoo.com/video/knicks-julius-randle-earns-second-004105516.html |access-date=March 22, 2022 |website=Yahoo News |archive-date=March 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220322224158/https://www.yahoo.com/video/knicks-julius-randle-earns-second-004105516.html |url-status=dead }} Randle struggled in the playoffs shooting 29 percent from the field, while the Knicks were beaten by the Atlanta Hawks in five games in the first round of the [[2021 NBA playoffs]], which was seen as a disappointment and Randle received flack from many analysts and fans.{{Cite web |title=Julius Randle Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/randlju01.html his contract on August 27, 2021, with a four-year, $117 million extension.{{cite web| url = https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31963913/julius-randle-agrees-4-year-117-million-extension-new-york-knicks| title = Julius Randle agrees to 4-year, $117 million extension with New York Knicks| web|url=https://nypost.com/2022/03/08/julius-randles-career-high-46-points-spark-knicks-win-over-kings/|title=Julius Randle's career-high 46 points spark huge Knicks rally in win over fans as a disappointment, especially after his prior playoff disappointment.{{cite web |last1=Partee |first1=Chris |title=Has it really been a bad year for Julius Randle or was last season just an outlier? |url=https://deadspin.com/has-it-really-been-a-bad-year-for-julius-randle-or-was-1848697334 |website=Deadspin |date=March 24, 2022 |access-date=15 April 2023}} [[File:Jalen Brunson - 52977333593 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Randle with the Knicks in 2023]] On December 28, 2022, Randle recorded 41 points, 11 rebounds and 7 assists in a 122–115 loss against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |title=Spurs overcome Randle's 41, hand Knicks fifth straight loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468682 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 25, 2023 |date=December 29, 2022}} On January 15, 2023, Randle put up 42 points and 15 rebounds in a 117–104 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He also became the first player in Knicks history to put up at least 40 points and 15 rebounds in a game since [[Patrick Ewing]] in 1996.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/knicks-news-julius-randle-joins-patrick-ewing-in-history-with-monster-performance-vs-pistons|title=Knicks' Julius Randle joins Patrick Ewing in history with monster performance vs. Pistons|website=ClutchPoints|last=Zavala|first=Steve|date=January 15, 2023|access-date=January 15, 2023}} On February 2, 2023, Randle was named to his second [[2023 NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star Game]] as a reserve for the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]].{{Cite web |title=2023 NBA All-Star reserves revealed |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-all-star-reserves-announced |access-date=2023-02-03 |website=NBA.com}} On February 24, Randle tied a then career-high 46 points in a 115–109 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/knicks-news-julius-randle-has-new-york-fans-hyped-after-dropping-46-on-wizards|title=Julius Randle has Knicks fans hyped after dropping 46 on Wizards|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=February 24, 2023|access-date=February 24, 2023}} On March 3, Randle scored 43 points, grabbed nine rebounds and made a game-winning three-pointer in a 122–120 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/knicks-news-julius-randle-sticks-knife-heats-hearts-epic-game-winner|title=WATCH: Knicks star Julius Randle sticks knife in Heat's hearts with cold-blooded game-winner|website=ClutchPoints|last=Songco|first=Paolo|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=March 3, 2023}} On March 20, in a 140–134 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Randle scored a career-high 57 points, going 19-of-29 from the field. His 57 points were the most by a Knick in a game since [[Carmelo Anthony]]'s franchise-record 62 points in [[2013–14 New York Knicks season|2014]].{{cite web |last1=Friedell |first1=Nick |title=Knicks' Julius Randle scores career-high 57 points in loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35907401/knicks-julius-randle-scores-career-high-57-points-loss |website=ESPN.com |date=March 21, 2023 |access-date=21 March 2023}} On March 30, the Knicks announced that Randle would be out for at least two weeks with a left ankle sprain, which he suffered during a game the day earlier against the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Knicks' Julius Randle Out 2 Weeks with Sprained Ankle Injury Ahead of NBA Playoffs |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10070703-knicks-julius-randle-out-2-weeks-with-sprained-ankle-injury-ahead-of-nba-playoffs |access-date=March 30, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}} Randle had an up and down playoff showing struggling with his shot but still being able to contribute to his team & help get them to the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Coming back from injury in Game 1 of the 1st Round vs the Cleveland Cavaliers, Randle had a strong showing scoring 19 points to go along with 10 rebounds, 4 assists & 2 steals in a win on the road. Randle also re-injured his ankle in Game 5 of the 1st Round. He missed Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals but played in Game 2, scoring 25 points, grabbing 12 rebounds and dishing out 8 assists in a win to tie the series.{{Cite web |title=Julius Randle struggles again in playoffs, changes needed for Knicks to progress {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/julius-randle-playoffs-struggle-again-changes-needed |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=NBA.com}} On February 1, 2024, Randle was named to his third [[2024 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] as an Eastern Conference reserve.{{Cite web |title=2024 NBA All-Star reserves announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-nba-all-star-reserves-announced |access-date=2024-02-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On April 4, it was announced that Randle will undergo shoulder surgery that would make him miss the remainder of the 2024 season.{{Cite web |title=Knicks' Julius Randle to Undergo Season-Ending Surgery on Shoulder Injury |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10115574-knicks-julius-randle-to-undergo-season-ending-surgery-on-shoulder-injury |access-date=2024-04-04 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2024–2026)=== On October 2, 2024, Randle was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] along with teammate [[Donte DiVincenzo]] as part of a three-team trade with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] that sent [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] to the Knicks.{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Forward Keita Bates-Diop, Guard Donte DiVincenzo and Forward Julius Randle from New York Knicks|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-forward-keita-bates-diop-guard-donte-divincenzo-and-forward-julius-randle-from-new-york-knicks|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 2, 2024}} On October 22, Randle made his Timberwolves debut, scoring 16 points, nine rebounds and four assists, in a 110–103 loss to his former team, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/nba-fans-slam-julius-randle-performance-in-timberwolves-lakers-game|title=NBA Fans Slam Julius Randle's Performance In Timberwolves-Lakers Game|website=Sports Illustrated|last=Stinar|first=Ben|date=October 23, 2024|access-date=November 17, 2024}} On November 17, Randle scored a game-winning 3-point [[Buzzer beater|buzzer-beater]] to give the Timberwolves a 120–117 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |date=November 18, 2024 |title=Randle hits 3 at the buzzer to lift Timberwolves over Booker, Suns with 120-117 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704800 |access-date=July 22, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}} He started 69 games for the Timberwolves during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 18.7 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 4.7 assists. In Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals, Randle recorded a triple-double with 24 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists in a 102–97 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He became the second Timberwolves player to record a playoff triple-double, after [[Kevin Garnett]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45092045/randle-does-all-triple-double-fuels-wolves-game-3|title=Randle does it all as triple-double fuels Wolves in Game 3|website=ESPN|last=McMenamin|first=Dave|date=May 11, 2025|access-date=May 11, 2025}} In Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals, Randle scored a playoff career-high 31 points in a 117–110 victory, helping the Timberwolves take a 3–1 series lead over the Warriors.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401769840|title=Edwards, Randle lead the way again as Timberwolves beat Warriors 117-110 for 3-1 playoff series lead|website=ESPN|date=May 13, 2025|access-date=May 13, 2025}} In Game 3 of the [[2025 NBA playoffs#(1) Oklahoma City Thunder vs. (6) Minnesota Timberwolves|Western Conference Finals]], Randle scored 24 points in a 143–101 blowout win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. The victory cut the Thunder's series lead to 2–1 and marked the Timberwolves’ highest-scoring playoff game in franchise history.{{cite web |title=Anthony Edwards and the Wolves strike back with 143-101 win to cut Thunder's West finals lead to 2-1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401773150 |website=ESPN.com |date=May 25, 2025 |access-date=May 25, 2025}}{{cite web |title=Randle's revival for Wolves in Game 3 rout starts with pep talk from Edwards |url=https://www.nba.com/news/julius-randle-game-3 |website=NBA.com |date=May 25, 2025 |access-date=May 25, 2025}} Minnesota went on to lose to Oklahoma City in five games. On June 29, 2025, Randle and the Timberwolves agreed to a three-year, $100 million contract extension.{{Cite web|title=Reports: Julius Randle, Wolves agree to 3-year, $100 million extension|url=https://www.nba.com/news/julius-randle-timberwolves-contract-extension-2025|access-date=October 3, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On March 25, 2026, Randle scored the game-winning jumper with 8.8 seconds remaining to seal the Timberwolves' come-from-behind 110–108 overtime win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. The Timberwolves' 13-point overtime comeback was the largest in the play-by-play era.{{cite web |author= |date=March 26, 2026 |title=Wolves surge past Rockets in overtime 110-108 on game-closing 15-0 run capped by Randle's winner |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810913 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=March 26, 2026}} === Brooklyn Nets (2026–present) === On July 10, 2026, Randle, alongside the draft rights to [[Joshua Jefferson]], was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] as part of a four-team trade in which the Timberwolves acquired [[LaMelo Ball]], [[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]] and the draft rights to [[Isaiah Evans]].{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Two-Time All-NBA Forward Julius Randle and Draft Rights to Joshua Jefferson in Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-two-time-all-nba-forward-julius-randle-and-draft-rights-to-joshua-jefferson-in-four-team-trade |access-date=July 10, 2026 |publisher=[[Brooklyn Nets]]}} ==National team career== In the 2016 off-season, Randle joined the US Select Team that practiced against the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States men's national team]] ahead of the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].{{cite web |title=D'Angelo Russell and Julius Randle join U.S. Olympic preparation |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=June 7, 2016 |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-sn-us-olympic-hoops-20160607-snap-story.html}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2014}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2014–15 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
